BRANNOCK HARBOUR, 14 March 2031 (Meridian Brief) — The lead vessel of the Isolde-class was formally accepted into service on Friday, carrying a certified capacity of 1,800 passengers, people familiar with the matter said.

The ferry can also take 420 vehicles across two decks, according to the same people.

Captain Marguerite Olvanger, Fleet Operations Director of the Halvorsen Strait Ferry Authority, confirmed the passenger figure at the handover ceremony.

The number appears in the Certificate of Passenger Capacity (Ref. HSFA-IC-0147), which was issued after the vessel completed acceptance trials at Brannock Harbour. People familiar with the matter said the certificate sets the limit for the ship's operation.

The Authority has not released a timetable for the vessel's first scheduled crossing.

Meridian Brief will update this item as further details become available.
